# Moonlighter (claude-auto-retry)

> Keep Claude Code working while you're away. Zero-dependency Node CLI plus a macOS menu bar
> app. When a usage/session limit hits ("You've hit your session limit · resets 2am"), it
> waits until the printed reset — including a weekly limit's date ("resets Oct 12, 2am") —
> and sends your continuation prompt. When the context window fills ("Context limit reached ·
> /compact or /clear to continue") it sends `/compact`, waits for compaction to finish, then
> continues. Sustained API overload (`API Error: 529 … overloaded_error`, 500/502/503/504) gets
> exponential backoff with jitter; safeguard/AUP false positives get a bounded immediate
> re-send. tmux-based, so it keeps working after you disconnect.

Install (from source — this fork is not published to npm; `npm i -g claude-auto-retry` installs
the upstream project, which lacks context-limit compaction, per-session prompts and the menu
bar app):

    git clone https://github.com/BansalAakash/moonlighter.git
    cd moonlighter
    ./install.sh

Then open a new terminal and use `claude` as usual. Check on it with
`claude-auto-retry status` (per-session state) and `claude-auto-retry logs`.

Key facts:

- Detects the real Claude Code renders verbatim: `5-hour limit reached - resets 3pm`,
  `You've hit your session limit · resets 2am (Europe/Zurich)`,
  `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Oct 9, 10am`, `Claude usage limit reached`,
  `You're out of extra usage`, `Context limit reached · /compact or /clear to continue`,
  `API Error: 529 {"type":"overloaded_error"…}`,
  `API Error: Server is temporarily limiting requests (not your usage limit)`,
  `<model>'s safeguards flagged this message`.
- Strict by design: a trigger must be a whole line in the live region of the pane, so text that
  merely quotes or discusses a limit never fires. Anything it is unsure about, it leaves alone.
- Navigates the `/rate-limit-options` menu to "Stop and wait for limit to reset" across any menu
  layout; never confirms "Upgrade your plan".
- Verifies Claude is the foreground process before injecting keys, and stands down the moment
  the user (or Claude) resumes.
- Timezone- and DST-aware reset-time parsing (including dated, multi-day resets); `--print`
  mode supported.
- Config is optional: `~/.claude-auto-retry.json`. Edits apply to running sessions within
  seconds; invalid JSON keeps the last good settings and logs a warning.
- Per-session resume prompts and an on/off switch per session, from the menu bar app.
- Everything runs locally: no account, no network calls, no runtime dependencies.
- bash, zsh and fish. macOS and Linux (the menu bar app is macOS 13+).

Docs:

- [README](https://github.com/BansalAakash/moonlighter/blob/main/README.md): install, overnight use, troubleshooting
- [Reference](https://github.com/BansalAakash/moonlighter/blob/main/docs/reference.md): every config key and the detection rules (inherited from upstream, with fork notes at the top)
- [Menu bar app](https://github.com/BansalAakash/moonlighter/blob/main/menubar/README.md)
- [Upstream DESIGN-NOTES](https://github.com/cheapestinference/claude-auto-retry/blob/master/DESIGN-NOTES.md): architecture of the StopFailure event channel vs. the terminal scraper

## Install for a user (agent-friendly)

- `git clone https://github.com/BansalAakash/moonlighter.git && cd moonlighter && ./install.sh`
  — links the CLI, installs the shell function (bash/zsh/fish) and the repair timer, and builds
  the menu bar app on macOS. Idempotent; re-run after switching Node versions. Takes effect in
  new shells.
- `claude-auto-retry install-hook` — optional: event-driven overload detection via Claude Code's
  StopFailure hook (edits `~/.claude/settings.json`, so it is not done automatically)
- Verify: `claude-auto-retry status`
- Remove: `claude-auto-retry uninstall` (and `uninstall-hook`, `uninstall-timer`)
